questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Madrid?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Spain is Madrid.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Spain?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Spain article.

questions.proof: The capital and most populous city is Madrid.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Spain?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the part of the article about the economy, or at the facts for the country.

questions.proof: The money used in Spain is the euro.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Spain about 505,990 square kilometres; Poland about 312,683 square kilometres; Senegal about 196,722 square kilometres; Republic of Ireland about 69,797 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Spain?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Spain on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Spain article.

questions.proof: Spain borders Portugal in the west, Andorra and France with the Pyrenees in the north, Gibraltar in the south, and Morocco with its overseas territories of Ceuta, Melilla, and the Peñón de Vélez de la Gomera.
